title: 26.1: A 24GHz Direct Digital Transmitter Using Multiphase Subharmonic Switching PA Achieving 3.2Gb/s Data Rate and -30.8dB EVM in 65nm CMOS
problem: Wide-bandwidth (multi-Gb/s) RF transmitters for K/Ka-band (24GHz) must achieve low EVM and high efficiency across peak and back-off power levels, but IQ summation causes 3dB power loss and prior subharmonic switching (SHS) designs were bandwidth-limited to tens of MHz.
motivation: 5G/radar systems require high-efficiency transmitters supporting spectrum-efficient modulations with high PAPR; back-off efficiency is critical for thermal management in antenna arrays.
method: Multiphase subharmonic switching (MP-SHS) transmitter architecture combines phase-shifted subharmonic LO divider (attenuating subharmonic spurs via phase shift), current-shared phase-interpolator MUX for MP LO generation, and dual-rate hybrid DAC with noise shaping to enable 3.2Gb/s operation at 24GHz while maintaining peak and PBO efficiency.
key_novelty: Multiphase SHS architecture mitigates both the 3dB IQ power loss and low PBO efficiency of prior approaches by distributing power across multiple phases while using phase-shifted subharmonic LO dividers to suppress spurs.
contributions: Multiphase SHS TX architecture improving both peak (22.3%) and PBO (20.3%) PAE simultaneously
Phase-shifted subharmonic LO divider scheme reducing subharmonic spurs via frequency-division phase shift
Current-shared phase-interpolator MUX technique with minimal overhead for MP LO generation
Dual-rate hybrid DAC enabling noise shaping and low in-band EVM (-30.8dB at 3.2Gb/s)

metrics.speedup: 3.2 Gb/s data rate (vs. tens of MHz in prior SHS work)

baselines: State-of-the-art K/Ka-band CMOS PA/TX (prior IQ and polar approaches)
limitations: Demonstration limited to 65nm CMOS at 24GHz; scalability to higher frequencies or newer nodes not discussed.
primary_theme: Multiphase subharmonic switching for high-efficiency wideband RF transmission
